summary: Ran all four acceptance checks against the built production server at http://localhost:3000/invoices. All four pass.
The heading reads exactly Invoices (5), matching the 5 rows in the table, and is served as plain HTML with no React comment markers.
The export button is untouched: it still reads Export 3 invoices as CSV and still downloads a 3-row CSV.

blocks.caption: Acceptance checks 1, 2 and 4 in one screenshot of the running app: the first heading reads Invoices (5), the table below it has 5 body rows (INV-1001 to INV-1005), and the button still reads Export 3 invoices as CSV.
Acceptance check 1, close up on the <h1>: the heading text is exactly Invoices (5), not Invoices.
Acceptance check 2: the five body rows counted on the page — INV-1001, INV-1002, INV-1003, INV-1004, INV-1005 — which is the 5 the heading shows.

Acceptance check 3: the HTML served by curl contains the literal

Invoices (5)

, and the whole document has zero markers. The hydrated DOM after a reload gives the same h1.innerHTML, so the single-template-literal rule holds server-side and after hydration.
Acceptance check 4: the export button after the heading change still reads Export 3 invoices as CSV — the heading's 5 counts rows listed, the button's 3 counts rows exported.

Acceptance check 4: the file Chromium actually downloaded when the button was clicked (invoices-2026-11-21.csv) — a header row plus three data rows, with the draft INV-1004 and the void INV-1005 absent. Clicking a second time downloaded it again.

blocks.title: Where the two numbers on the page come from
blocks.mermaid:
flowchart LR

blocks.caption: Before and after of the changed lines: the count is interpolated from invoices.length — the same array <tbody> maps over — in one template literal, not a hardcoded 5 and not exportable.length.

A second route into the same screen: navigating from / via the Go to invoices link (client-side, no full page load) renders the same Invoices (5) heading, 5 rows and 3-invoice button, with no comment markers in the h1 and no console errors.

focus.title: The heading number is derived, not written down
focus.detail: The heading reads Invoices (5) because it interpolates invoices.length, the array the table body maps over. Nothing here hardcodes 5, and nothing adds a status filter — so if a filter is added to that array later the heading follows it.

focus.title: No React comment markers in the served HTML
focus.detail:
The count is in a single template literal, so the server renders

Invoices (5)

. curl of the page finds zero markers anywhere in the document, and the hydrated DOM's h1.innerHTML is the same plain string. The page hydrates with no console errors.

focus.title: The export path is unchanged
focus.detail: The button still reads Export 3 invoices as CSV, and clicking it still fetches /invoices/export (200, text/csv; charset=utf-8, Content-Disposition attachment, Cache-Control no-store) and downloads a CSV of 3 invoices. A second click downloads it again. The two numbers on the page, 5 and 3, are deliberately different.
